outcome: lung aeration (LUS grade, CoV of pixel intensity)
oxygen exchange capacity (Alveolar-arterial difference in oxygen; AaDO2)
cohort: Nineteen near-term (140 days gestation) spontaneously breathing lambs were studied, divided into a control group with normal lung liquid levels and an experimental group with elevated lung liquid levels.
finding: Lung ultrasound (LUS) can monitor lung aeration and liquid clearance after birth in spontaneously breathing near-term lambs, and quantitative image analysis (CoV) can detect differences in lung aeration that qualitative LUS grading may miss, especially with lung liquid retention.
mod_finding: All lambs in the study were delivered by Caesarean section.
